A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GeoBridge and GeoLoc. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables and figures can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Sections 5.2–5.4 report original cross-view and cross-modal retrieval results, qualitative examples and alignment ablations.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and appendix Section 8 adds text-generator validation and experiments on a three-view public-data subset.

M1.justification: The CLIP-based encoders, semantic-anchor alignment, combined contrastive objective and retrieval procedure remain unchanged. Alternative text generators are tested as experimental configurations rather than introduced as a revised core method.

E1.justification: Section 8.2 and Table 10 add a subset identified as CVUSA with drone, panorama and satellite views, extending its evaluated coverage beyond the retained street–satellite setting. All original datasets and tasks remain.

E2.justification: Table 9 adds Qwen3-generated, Gemini3-generated and ensemble-generated semantic-anchor variants as comparisons with the standard configuration. Retrieval baselines in the original experiments are unchanged; Table 10 reuses existing baseline methods.

E3.justification: The new subset experiment uses 750×750 drone crops, 481 image sets with 81 reserved for testing, and projection-layer-only fine-tuning. These are additional experimental settings; the original benchmark training and evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 9 adds targeted sensitivity checks for the text generator and ensemble descriptions. Section 8.2 tests dependence on the data source through public-subset retraining. The original alignment ablation and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, training seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for its experiments. The added tables continue reporting point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 retain their numerical entries. Table 9 adds generator-dependent results, including Qwen3 D2S R@1 of 46.07 versus 45.05 for the standard configuration. Table 10 adds subset results, including GeoBridge D2S R@1/AP of 49.38/62.46; these are not revisions to the original CVUSA scores.

T1.justification: The problem formulation and mathematical objectives in Equations 1–6 are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The semantic-anchor contribution, bidirectional retrieval capabilities, GeoLoc novelty and scale, and accuracy/generalization claims remain. Several passages replace 'foundation model' with 'model' or 'framework', but no explicit capability scope changes, and the title retains the original terminology.

C2.justification: Sections 4 and 8 explicitly argue that effectiveness is not specific to GPT-4o or a proprietary data source. The existing limitations concerning geographic coverage, filtering, acquisition conditions and generated-text biases remain unchanged, moving from Section 12 to Section 13.

D1.justification: v2 identifies OpenAerialMap as the drone-image source, adds source/API-policy links and documents the new subset construction and fine-tuning settings. The abstract changes resource release from completed to forthcoming; this changes the stated access status without establishing actual resource withdrawal.

R1.justification: Eight cited works are added, including Qwen3, Gemini and remote-sensing/LLM research such as GeoEyes and GeoZero. These support background statements and new experiments without substantially changing the positioning against satellite-centric localization.

P1.justification: There are limited terminology, affiliation and wording edits, deletion of a short explanatory passage, and insertion of supplementary Section 8 with subsequent renumbering. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: Two full-width supplementary tables are added. Existing tables and surrounding text are repositioned, including Table 6 moving from page 6 to page 7. Figures 1–17 retain their content; the document undergoes reflow rather than a visual redesign.

improvement.justification: The generator-sensitivity experiment, public-subset evaluation and newly disclosed drone-image source modestly strengthen validation and provenance. Their benefit is limited by sparse new-protocol details and the 81-example test set; Section 8.2 also names CVUSA while citing the reference assigned to CVACT. The core method and original results remain unchanged.
